key_insight: Retention-constrained fine-tuning improves an aluminium MACE potential’s defect predictions while preserving its tested near-equilibrium mechanical response.
engineering_relevance: The protocol supports more reliable atomistic simulations of aluminium defect dynamics and plasticity without sacrificing validated bulk behaviour.
method: Select configurations using conditional force uncertainty over 144 readout weights, with within-batch covariance updates.
Iteratively update all model parameters while anchoring historical relative energies.
Gate updates against historical energy and vibrational tolerances.
evidence_signal: After four rounds, 32 acquired configurations and 400 gradient updates, development force error fell from 22.43 to 21.52 meV/Å, outperforming sampling baselines; all three force-uncertainty runs met bulk-retention criteria, with phonon RMS drift below 0.05 THz.
watch_item: Retention is demonstrated only for the tested aluminium configurations and tolerances; broader transfer and closed-loop robustness require further validation.
paper_title: Retention-constrained fine-tuning of a pre-trained aluminium MACE potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity
